text.tspan: The 68901 MFP also provides a slow speed RS-232C serial port to the system. The baud rate
clock for the MFP serial port transmitter and receiver is derived from the timer D output of
the MFP. Given the MFP's 2.4576 MHz clock, baud rates up to 19.2Kbaud can be supported.
The MFP serial port is connected to a DB-9P connector and contains a complete complement of
The parallel interface is implemented through the programmable sound generator chip. It is a
subset of the Centronics standard and is output to a DB25 connector. The Centronics STROBE
signal is generated from the PSG bit. The Centronics BUSY signal is connected to one of the
parallel input lines of the MFP to permit interrupt driven printing. Eight bits of read/write data
are handled through I/O port B on the PSG at a typical transfer rate exceeding 4 Kbytes per
